correctness.rationale: For a centered geodesic sphere, all principal curvatures equal \(\cot\rho\), so the flow reduces exactly to \(\rho'=-\gamma_0\rho^{a+1}A(\rho)\) with \(A(\rho)=(\rho\cot\rho)^{k\alpha}=1-(k\alpha/3)\rho^2+O(\rho^4)\). With \(x=\rho^{-a}\), \(L=1+a\gamma_0t\), and \(E=x-L\), one has \(dE/dL=A(\rho)-1\), \(x/L\to1\), and hence \(\rho^2=L^{-2/a}(1+o(1))\). Integrating gives the power, logarithmic, and convergent-tail regimes exactly at \(a=2\); expanding \(y=(1+E/L)^{-1/a}\) gives the stated constants. In the resonant case the factor \(\log L=2\log\lambda\) exactly cancels \(1/a=1/2\). The subcritical integral has local integrand \(-(k\alpha/3)r^{1-a}+O(r^{3-a})\), so it converges precisely for \(a<2\).
residual_risks: The theorem is only for the invariant centered round family; no nonspherical second-order mode claim is audited.

final_claim: Let \(1\le k\le n\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(\beta>1+k\alpha\). For the centered geodesic-sphere solution of \(\partial_tX=-\rho^\beta\sigma_k^\alpha\nu\) in the unit sphere, put \(a=\beta-k\alpha-1\), \(\gamma_0=\binom{n}{k}^\alpha\), \(\lambda(t)=(1+a\gamma_0t)^{1/a}\), \(y(t)=\lambda(t)\rho(t)\), and \(B=k\alpha/3\). Then \(y(t)\to1\), with \(\lambda^2(y-1)\to B/(a-2)\) for \(a>2\), \(\lambda^2(y-1)/\log\lambda\to B\) for \(a=2\), and \(\lambda^a(y-1)\to C(\rho_0)\) for \(0<a<2\), with the explicit convergent integral coefficient stated in RESULT.md.
limitations: The theorem concerns only centered geodesic spheres and does not determine nonspherical second-order modes.
